extra.message: The 'host' value comes directly from request.GET.get('host', ...) and is concatenated into a shell command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' or '`id`') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

pickle.loads() is called on 'raw', which is derived directly from request.body or the 'blob' GET/POST parameter (optionally base64-decoded). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted pickle payload (e.g. using __reduce__).

The 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This is a classic Server-Side Template Injection: an attacker can supply Jinja2 syntax (e.g. "{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}") to achieve remote code execution.

The lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, then used to parse raw request.body. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, allowing an attacker to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via crafted DTDs/entities.
